_comment: Task-type -> {model, effort} routing for the AI Implementation Factory. Human-readable rationale in PLAN.md §4. Models: claude-opus-4-8 (hard reasoning), claude-sonnet-4-6 (mid), claude-haiku-4-5 (cheap/fast), claude-fable-5 (top, budget-gated). effort: low|medium|high|xhigh|max. Driver reads this and passes opts {model, effort} per agent() call. Tune from real cost data after Phase 5. REVIEW STAGE = role gates (gate.*) + every BMAD review-named flow (review.*: code/adversarial/edgecase/testreview/editorial_structure/editorial_prose/nfr), each a separate adversarial subagent; 'when' = applicability (see config/factory.config.json reviewFlows); 'skill' = the bmad-* skill the agent invokes.

planner._ki_d11: fable-5 experiment 2026-07-19 (FABLE-PROBE-OK re-verified access, reversing KI-C8). Sets each non-trivial item's whole approach; opus/high fallback (KI-D10) preserves prior routing on a fable outage.

archaeologist._ki_e460: research phase — establishes validated ground truth for a doc-less legacy target BEFORE planning. Deliberately off the budget-gated fable-5 tier: on a genuinely doc-less host this can fire on close to every non-mechanical item's first touch of each target, so it needs a cost-predictable default, not an experimental one.

planner.mechanical._note: KI-E440: mechanical planner downgraded high->medium. A mechanical item is bounded by definition; the plan decides the approach for haiku hands, not a full novel-reasoning pass. KI-E469 (owner directive "haiku as the hands, sonnet as the developer brains") — mechanical items previously had NO planner at all, so routing the mechanical fixer/test-author to haiku would have produced hands with no brain in front of them. This route gives the mechanical tier its own planner.

fixer.mechanical._note: KI-E468 (2026-09-02 owner directive; supersedes the KI-E92 sonnet-4-6 re-adoption): haiku is the hands for mechanical fixes, sonnet is the developer brains (planner.mechanical above, consolidation below).

fixer.steps.critical._note: KI-E473 (owner directive "for non trivial tasks - sonnet can be used for steps") — the STEP calls of a KI-E470 stepwise run on the CRITICAL tier. Each step is a single, bounded, individually-checkable unit executed against a plan that already exists and with the full roster in view, so it does not need the top authoring tier; the two passes that DO hold the whole item — the fable-5 planner and the opus-4-8 consolidation — are unchanged. Deliberately NOT `fixer.critical`: that route still serves the non-stepwise single whole-item call and all three bounded amends, which are whole-diff work and must stay on opus.

fixer.consolidation._note: KI-E472 — the KI-E470 stepwise CONSOLIDATION pass is whole-item reasoning across the complete diff (sibling-pattern sweep, dead-code trace, adjacent-claim re-check, CancellationToken chain, cross-step coherence), strictly harder than any individual step. Running it on the same cheap tier as the granular hands would put the least capable model on the one pass that has to hold the ENTIRE change in view. Applies to the MECHANICAL tier only when stepwise has 2+ steps; a non-trivial item's MULTI-step consolidation stays on opus-4-8 (`fixer.consolidation.solo` below covers the single-step case for both tiers).

fixer.consolidation.solo._note: KI-E487 (owner observation "one step small fixes would [not] require opus") — a plan that decomposed into exactly ONE step has no cross-step drift to reconcile — the specific hazard `fixer.consolidation`'s opus routing exists to catch on the CRITICAL tier. A single-step diff still deserves the sibling-pattern/dead-code/adjacent-claim sweep, just not at opus prices when there is only one pass to reconcile with itself. A plan with 2+ steps is UNCHANGED: its consolidation still resolves to `fixer.consolidation` via the tier-based route, never this one.

runner._ki_l64: pinned haiku->sonnet 2026-07-16: haiku 200k ceiling dies 'Prompt is too long' on big-solution verify; KI-L56 class, KI-L58 pin precedent

review.code._note: KI-E386a: downgraded from opus; LIGHT-band items already use SONNET; gate.security at opus still guards FULL-band CRITICAL items.

review.adversarial.mechanical._note: KI-E253 (owner directive): review.adversarial ran on opus for EVERY item regardless of complexity — the single largest concentration of opus spend in the whole gate band. Split by the SAME fixType!=mechanical signal used everywhere else for this judgment call.

review.editorial_prose._note: KI-L58 (2026-07-15): pinned haiku->sonnet — haiku's 200k ceiling dies terminal ('Prompt is too long') on doc-heavy items; KI-L56 context-ceiling class, KI-L49 pin precedent.

review.nfr._note: KI-E249/KI-E253 — advisory (blocking:false in factory.config.json), own tier since the effort drop. This pass never blocks an item on its own, so the cost of an occasional miss is a lot lower than a blocking gate's.

refuterLight._note: KI-E386b: MEDIUM/LOW/non-CRITICAL items use the mid-tier model for refutation instead of opus. Routing is severity-conditional in factory.js routesFor(): CRITICAL|HIGH -> refuter (opus), else refuterLight. NOT in a drift-guarded map so the live engine (factory.js) stays authoritative.

adjudicator._note: KI-D11 (2026-07-19): routed to its DESIGNED model fable-5/max — access re-verified (FABLE-PROBE-OK), reversing the cycle-6 access-gate that had forced opus/max. opus/max fallback (KI-D10) restores the prior behaviour on a fable outage. The hardest call in the factory (a disputed FULL-band split) — the strongest fable candidate.

concurrency.note: ONE workflow at a time; opus throttles harder than sonnet; per-agent retry>=3

budget.note: KI-C2 (2026-07-12): there is NO default cap (owner ruling — observability, not a governor). Enforcement engages ONLY when the operator sets a token budget on the LAUNCH TURN (a '+500k'-style directive): the Workflow runtime's `budget` global then hard-throws once spent >= total, and factory.js's graceful half refuses to START a new item when remaining() < reserve (item stays CLAIMED, no attempt burned, `resume` prints its relaunch line). `reserve` here is injected into runArgs at group/sweep emit.
